source.provider: Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources / National Fisheries Research and Development Institute

acquisition.storage: Ignored local research cache only; the PDF is not added to tracked files or app assets.

reportedStudy.samplingAndAnalysis: Random fish specimens were collected monthly from ring-net catches unloaded at nine selected landing sites. Monthly length-frequency data were pooled across the sites and raised for analysis; the article describes collection as approximately 10-11 days per month at most sites and 20-21 days at PFDA Market 3 and Fisherman's Wharf.

methodsLabelAnomaly.reviewFinding: This apparent genus-level typo conflicts with the abstract, introduction and results, which report Rastrelliger brachysoma. Do not treat the methods wording as a fourth taxon.

localityAssessment.sourceWording: The article describes the fish as Manila Bay ring-net catches and maps nine landing sites, including four in Cavite.
localityAssessment.captureSiteCrosswalk: Absent. Monthly length-frequency data were pooled across all nine landing sites; no species-by-landing-site allocation, capture-ground coordinate, capture date by taxon, or tow/voucher crosswalk is provided.
localityAssessment.interpretation: A named landing site is where a vessel unloads catch and does not by itself locate where the fish was captured. Retain this only as historical, source-reported Manila Bay fishery context; do not assign the taxa to Rosario, Tanza, Naic, Labac or any specific municipal water.
localityAssessment.geometry: The figure is an illustrative map of landing-site locations, not species capture coordinates, survey stations, or a legal bay/municipal-water boundary.

taxonomicCaveat: Preserve Sardinella fimbriata as the 2014 source label. Hata and Motomura (2019) described S. pacifica from Philippine specimens, and the 2025 type-locality checklist reports that most of its type specimens had previously been identified as S. fimbriata. This makes the old fishery name a taxonomic follow-up lead, but the 2014 NFRDI data are pooled and have no specimen/voucher crosswalk to the later type-series redetermination. Do not rename the 2014 fishery sample as S. pacifica without direct voucher or archived-sample evidence. The apparent methods typo and item-specific reuse issue also remain open.

rightsReview.itemSpecificReuse: Pending. The repository item metadata and reviewed PDF did not state an item-specific license. Current journal policy is not assumed to govern this 2017 item retroactively.
rightsReview.decision: No species table, figure, exact catch-composition table, species assertion, or public-app row is approved by this review.

decision.reason: The source supports historical Manila Bay ring-net fishery context and names three source taxa, but its length-frequency data are pooled across nine landing sites. Later taxonomic literature distinguishes Sardinella pacifica from S. fimbriata and records Manila Bay type material, but does not crosswalk the 2014 NFRDI fishery sample to those specimens. Landing locations do not resolve capture origins, and item-specific reuse remains unresolved.

nextAction: Seek a direct voucher, sample-ID, or archive crosswalk for the 2014 pooled Sardinella fimbriata label and clarify the apparent methods typo and item-specific reuse. Preserve the source name unless this direct crosswalk is obtained; no taxon-by-site or current-presence inference follows.
